paper.title: The End of Optimism? An Asymptotic Analysis of Finite-Armed Linear Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-armed stochastic linear bandit with Gaussian noise
unmapped: Noise is standard Gaussian N(0,1) (relaxable to 1-subgaussian for the upper bound)
settings.definition_quote: Let $\mathcal A \subset \R^d$ be a finite set that spans $\R^d$ with $|\mathcal A| = k$ and $\norm{x}_2 \leq 1$ for all $x \in \cA$. A learner interacts with the bandit over $n$ rounds. In each round $t$ the learner chooses an action (arm) $A_t \in \mathcal A$ and observes a payoff $Y_t = \inner{A_t, \theta} + \eta_t$ where $\eta_t \sim \mathcal N(0,1)$ is Gaussian noise and $\theta \in \R^d$ is an unknown parameter.

algorithms.name: Optimal Algorithm (Algorithm 1: warm-up / success / recovery phases)

bound.regime: n -> infinity; holds for each suboptimal x

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: Fix $\theta\in \R^d$ such that there is a unique optimal arm. Let $\pi$ be a consistent policy and let $\bar G_n = \E[\sum_{t=1}^n A_t A_t^\top]$, which we assume is invertible for sufficiently large $n$. Then for all suboptimal $x \in \mathcal A$ it holds that $\limsup_{n\to\infty} \log(n) \norm{x-x^*}_{\bar G_n^{-1}}^2 \leq \frac{\Delta_x^2}{2}$.

results.notes: This is a necessary condition on exploration (an upper limit on the confidence width log(n)||x-x*||^2_{G_n^{-1}}), not a direct regret bound. It is recorded as a lower-bound-type result with quantity 'other'.

symbols.c_A_theta: value of the optimisation problem: inf over alpha>=0 of sum_{x suboptimal} alpha(x) Delta_x subject to ||x||^2_{H(alpha)^{-1}} <= Delta_x^2/2 for all suboptimal x, with H(alpha)=sum_x alpha(x) x x^T

source.label: cor:regretlb
source.quote: Let $\pi$ be a consistent policy, $\theta\in \R^d$ such that there is a unique optimal arm in $\cA$. Then $\limsup_{n\to\infty} \log(n) \norm{x}_{\bar G_n^{-1}}^2 \leq \frac{\Delta_x^2}{2}$ and also $\limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{R_\theta^\pi(n)}{\log(n)} \geq c(\mathcal A, \theta)$, where $c(\mathcal A, \theta)$ is defined as the solution to the following optimisation problem...

results.notes: The statement is limsup R/log(n) >= c(A,theta). It is encoded here as limsup with expression c*log(T). The appendix proof actually gives a liminf version.

symbols.c_A_theta: optimal asymptotic constant from Corollary 2's optimisation problem

source.label: thm:upper
source.quote: Assuming that $x^*$ is unique, the strategy given in Algorithm \ref{alg:optimal} satisfies $\limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{R^\pi_\theta(n)}{\log(n)} \leq c(\mathcal A, \theta) \text{ for all } \theta \in \R^d$.

results.notes: The algorithm takes the horizon n as input. It matches the lower bound, so it is asymptotically optimal. The paper does not discuss the per-round cost of solving the optimisation problem.
